definition: In American politics since the 2020s, political figures have deployed AI-generated images, videos, and audio to attack opponents, create misleading narratives, or inflame emotions.
details: The use of generative AI by American political figures has been subject to criticism from many sides of the political spectrum. President Donald Trump has used generative AI in several posts to Truth Social during his second term, many of which have made headlines due to their inflammatory nature.

explainer.lead: AI-generated content has become part of American political campaigning and messaging, letting politicians and their allies manufacture convincing scenes, voices, and personas. It can make an attack faster and more attention-grabbing, but it can also mislead voters and weaken confidence that political media shows real events.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a computer that can draw any poster, make a pretend movie, or copy someone’s voice almost like a costume and puppet show. American politicians and campaigns have used these inventions to praise themselves, mock opponents, or tell stories that never happened. That matters because people watching online may think the costume and puppet show are real.
tiers.practitioner: In practice, the workflow combines generative media tools—Sora is one documented example—with campaign advertisements, robocalls, Truth Social, and other social channels. The main pitfalls are fabricated people or endorsements, undisclosed deepfakes, invented citations, and low-quality “AI slop” produced for attention and engagement. Audience belief cannot be assumed either way: some viewers did not recognize synthetic welfare videos, while others recognized them but still valued their political narrative.
tiers.paperLevel: The phenomenon can be expressed as G(x) → m → d, where a generative model produces political media m and a campaign, official, influencer, or anonymous account distributes it d. Documented functions include attack advertising, fabricated endorsements, emotional provocation, engagement farming, voter discouragement, and political fundraising through donor analysis. The category covers both parties and does not imply uniform deception or audience gullibility, although undisclosed synthetic media and fabricated references create distinct evidentiary problems.

explainer.example: In April 2023, the Republican National Committee released an attack advertisement made entirely with AI-generated images, depicting a dystopian future following Joe Biden’s re-election. The pictures did not need to document an actual future event to communicate the campaign’s warning.

usedIn.name: Truth Social
usedIn.detail: Donald Trump has shared AI-generated images and videos there, including self-aggrandizing portraits and attacks during protests.

usedIn.name: Campaign advertising
usedIn.detail: Campaigns and political groups have used synthetic scenes and deepfake opponents in television and online advertisements.

usedIn.name: Political robocalls
usedIn.detail: A Democratic consultant used AI-generated Biden audio in 2024 to discourage voter participation.

usedIn.name: Sora-generated social videos
usedIn.detail: Anonymous users posted fabricated welfare-abuse scenes during the 2025 government shutdown.

explainer.intuition: Generative AI removes the need for a real photograph, recording, or event before a political message can look or sound authentic. The same speed and flexibility that help campaigns produce content also make fabricated evidence and invented people cheap to distribute.
howItWorks: A political actor chooses a message, target, or emotion.
Generative tools produce images, video, or audio.
The media is packaged as a post, advertisement, robocall, or persona.
Social sharing and coverage amplify it, sometimes without viewers recognizing it as synthetic.
explainer.whyItMatters: Synthetic media can fabricate endorsements, discourage voting, inflame reactions, and supply false supporting references, drawing criticism from across the political spectrum. Misinformation experts have warned that repeated official use could erode the public’s shared perception of truth.
misconceptions: It is not confined to Republicans or Democrats; members of both parties have used generative AI.
Not every political use is deceptive media; campaigns have also used AI to analyze donor data.
It need not be polished or realistic, since low-quality “AI slop” can still farm attention and engagement.
